New hospitals for the East · Phase 1

Try the jobs that build and run the East’s new hospitals

Five new hospitals are being built in Norfolk, Suffolk, Cambridgeshire and Milton Keynes. Free virtual work experience (VWE) lets you try both sides: the construction careers that build each hospital and the NHS careers that run it. Twelve VWEs, six to build it and six to run it, each leading to a real apprenticeship, T Level or degree route.

Two industries, one hospital

Every new hospital needs two workforces

Construction teams design, make and build the hospital. NHS teams plan it, move in and care for patients for decades. Some careers sit in both worlds, and those are some of the most in-demand jobs of all.

Construction

Build the hospital

Architects, engineers, site managers, electricians, bricklayers, plant operators and factory teams making standard hospital parts offsite under the Hospital 2.0 approach.

See construction careers →
Both

Bridge the two

Healthcare planners, medical gas engineers, clinical engineers, commissioning teams and estates managers turn a building into a working hospital.

See bridge careers →
NHS

Run the hospital

Nurses, doctors, allied health professionals, healthcare scientists, pharmacy teams, porters, caterers, data analysts and managers, many with paid apprenticeships.

See NHS careers →

Inclusive by design

Every learner can take part

The same inclusion and adaptation tools are built into Developing Experts lessons and VWEs and into this microsite, so every learner can take part: those with SEND, dyslexia or visual stress, Deaf learners, and families who speak another language at home.

Jargon buster

What the words mean

Plain-English meanings for the terms used on this site.

VWE (virtual work experience)
Online work experience. You watch films, answer quizzes and make decisions in simulations set by real employers, and earn a certificate.
Apprenticeship
A paid job with training. You earn a wage, study part of the week and gain a qualification, with no tuition fees.
Foundation apprenticeship
A level 2 apprenticeship for 16 to 21 year olds (up to 24 in some cases) that gives a broad start in a sector, such as construction or health and social care.
Apprenticeship levels
Level 2 is like GCSEs, level 3 like A levels, levels 4 and 5 like the first years of a degree, level 6 a degree and level 7 a master’s degree.
Degree apprenticeship
A level 6 or 7 apprenticeship where you earn a full degree while working, with no student debt.
T Level
A two-year course after GCSEs, equal to three A levels, with a 45-day industry placement. Examples: Health, and Design, Surveying and Planning for Construction.
Apprenticeship standard
The official description of an apprenticeship job: what you need to know and be able to do. Each VWE is mapped to these.
Evidence report
The report you get after a VWE. It shows what you did and the skills you showed, and you can use it when you apply.
Gatsby Benchmarks
Eight national standards for good careers education in schools and colleges. VWEs help schools meet them.
RAAC
Reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete: a lightweight concrete used in some hospitals built decades ago that is now past its safe life. Four of the five hospitals are being replaced for this reason.
Hospital 2.0
The national approach to building hospitals with standard designs and more parts made in factories, so they are quicker and better to build.
New Hospital Programme
The government programme building new hospitals across England. The five hospitals here are in its first wave.
NHS trust
The NHS organisation that runs a hospital, such as West Suffolk NHS Foundation Trust.
Agenda for Change
The NHS pay system. Most NHS jobs sit in a numbered pay band, from band 2 to band 9.
CSCS card
The card most building sites ask to see, showing you have passed a health and safety test.
NEET
Not in education, employment or training. Usually used about 16 to 24 year olds.
Commissioning
Testing every system in a new building, such as power, air and medical gases, before patients arrive.
Social value
The extra good a big project does for local people, such as jobs, training and work with schools.

Questions people ask

What is virtual work experience?

Online work experience where you try a real job through films, quizzes and simulations set by the trusts and construction partners. Each of the 12 VWEs runs as a five-day, 25-hour placement for KS4 and KS5, or a 30-minute career taster that spotlights one career. You earn a certificate and an evidence report you can use to apply. See the VWEs.

Which hospitals are in Phase 1 in the East?

James Paget University Hospital in Gorleston, The Queen Elizabeth Hospital in King's Lynn, West Suffolk Hospital in Bury St Edmunds, Hinchingbrooke Hospital in Huntingdon and Milton Keynes University Hospital. All five are in Wave 1 of the national New Hospital Programme.

Why are four of them being replaced?

James Paget, Queen Elizabeth, West Suffolk and Hinchingbrooke were built largely with reinforced autoclaved aerated concrete (RAAC), which has reached the end of its life. Milton Keynes is a major new development on its existing site, including maternity, children's services and extra surgical capacity.

When will the jobs start?

Design and planning roles are under way now. Construction activity ramps up from 2027 onwards, and the NHS will recruit for new and changed roles in the run-up to each hospital opening. Many NHS roles are open now at each trust.

What is Hospital 2.0?

A standard way to design and build hospitals, with repeatable designs and more parts made in factories offsite. That creates manufacturing, digital and logistics jobs as well as traditional site work.

Do I need a degree?

No. Many roles start with an apprenticeship, a T Level or on-the-job training, including healthcare assistant, porter, pharmacy technician, electrician, plumber and plant operator. Nursing, many allied health roles and engineering can also be reached by a degree apprenticeship, so you earn while you learn.

I'm an adult changing career. Is it too late?

No. Apprenticeships have no upper age limit, and skills from trades, driving, the forces, retail and care count. Search NHS Jobs and the construction partners' careers pages, and ask the local college about funded courses and Skills Bootcamps.

      Money words explained

      Gross pay

      Your pay before anything is taken off.

      Take-home (net) pay

      What reaches your bank account after tax, National Insurance, pension and any student loan.

      Personal allowance

      The first £12,570 you earn each year is tax-free.

      Income tax

      20% on earnings from £12,570 to £50,270 (basic rate), 40% above (higher rate). Your tax code tells your employer how much allowance you get, usually 1257L.

      National Insurance

      8% on earnings between £12,570 and £50,270, then 2%. It counts towards your State Pension.

      Pension

      Money saved for later life. In the NHS Pension Scheme you pay 5.2% to 12.5% and your employer adds 23.7%. Other employers must add at least 3%.

      Student loan

      You only repay once you earn over the threshold: 9% of earnings above £29,385 (Plan 2) or £25,000 (Plan 5). It stops when you earn less, and is written off after 30 or 40 years.

      Agenda for Change band

      The NHS pay scale for most staff, from Band 2 to Band 9. Most bands have pay points you move up with experience.

      Unsocial hours

      Extra NHS pay for evenings, nights, weekends and bank holidays, as a percentage of your hourly rate.

      Overtime

      Hours worked above your normal week. In construction it is often paid at time and a half.

      Council tax

      A local tax on your home, paid monthly to the council. If you live alone you get 25% off.

      Lifetime ISA

      A savings account for a first home for people aged 18 to 39. The government adds 25% to up to £4,000 a year.

      Estimates only, not financial advice. Minimum wage rates are the GOV.UK rates from 1 April 2026; the Real Living Wage of £14.10 was announced by the Living Wage Foundation on 15 October 2026. Pension projections are illustrative, in today’s money, and not guaranteed. NHS pay uses the 2026/27 Agenda for Change rates for England, with NHS Pension Scheme member rates from 1 April 2026 and the 23.7% employer rate. Unsocial hours pay is a rough estimate that depends on your shifts. Construction pay is an example range to be confirmed with the construction partners, with a 5% auto-enrolment pension and a 3% employer contribution. Take-home uses 2026/27 income tax and National Insurance for England with the standard personal allowance, and 2026/27 student loan thresholds. Rents, council tax and house prices are rounded typical figures for each hospital town from ONS and local listings in 2026; check local listings. Mortgage figures assume a 5% deposit, 30 years and 4.5% interest; real offers depend on your circumstances. Your choices are saved in this browser only.

        In-demand roles

        Which jobs does the region need most?

        Each role gets a demand score out of 100 from five signals: live vacancies, what the hospital programme needs, workforce gaps, retirements and how few people are training for it. Use it to choose a VWE with strong job prospects, or to plan training and recruitment.

        Illustrative scores. Live vacancies come from the jobs board; the other signals are example values. The live system takes them from the data sources listed below.

        How the score works, and adjust it

        Each signal is scored 0 to 100, then combined using the weights below. Move a slider to change how much a signal counts. Critical is 72 or more, High 63 to 71, Rising 54 to 62, and anything lower is Steady.

        Data sources for the live system

        • Live vacancies: the partner API feeds on this site (NHS Jobs, Find an apprenticeship, partner careers sites), plus regional job-postings data
        • Programme need: the construction partners' labour plans for each hospital, by trade and month
        • Workforce gap: NHS England vacancy statistics by staff group and region; CITB Construction Skills Network forecast for the East of England
        • Retirement risk: NHS workforce age profiles from the trusts; industry age data
        • Pipeline: VWE completions on this site, plus college, apprenticeship and university starts
        • Local priorities: the Local Skills Improvement Plans for Norfolk and Suffolk, Cambridgeshire and Peterborough, and South East Midlands

        ▶ VWE 1

        Roles: Dryliner, Floor layer, Painter and decorator

        Help to apply

        Support for job seekers

        Whether you are leaving school, out of work, changing career or coming back to work, here is how to get from a VWE to a job offer.

        Leaving school or college
        • Do the VWE for the job you want
        • Look for apprenticeships and T Level placements
        • Ask your college about the partner near you
        Your route →
        Out of work
        • Talk to your work coach about the jobs here
        • Many roles train you from day one
        • Free courses and Skills Bootcamps may be funded
        Find a course ↗
        Starting on a building site
        • Most sites ask for a CSCS card
        • Take the health, safety and environment test
        • The VWE covers site safety basics
        CSCS cards ↗
        Working in a hospital
        • NHS roles are advertised on NHS Jobs
        • Many patient-facing roles need a DBS check
        • Healthcare assistant roles often need no experience
        NHS Jobs ↗
        Disabled job seekers
        • Tell us about adjustments when you apply
        • Ask employers about Disability Confident
        • The VWEs work with screen readers and BSL
        Accessibility settings →
        Career changers, veterans and returners
        • Your skills from other jobs count
        • Apprenticeships have no upper age limit
        • Use your evidence report instead of a CV
        See the evidence report →

        Talent pool

        Learners aged 16+ who opted in to hear about your roles. Identities stay hidden until a learner accepts; every contact goes through Developing Experts.
        Consent firstUnder-16s appear only as anonymous totals. Learners 16+ choose to join the pool and can leave at any time.
        Mediated contactInvitations go through the learner's Developing Experts account, and their school or college is told.
        Fair by designReadiness comes from the VWE evidence report, not school or postcode. A recruiter always decides.
